properties.statement:
112 OF 205 TEMPORAL FACTS CARRY A DATE NOTHING READS — AND THE OTHER 76 CARRY IT SOMEWHERE ELSE. ZERO CARRY BOTH.

MEASURED on reflow2's own committed export, 2026-08-16:
  205 TemporalFacts
  112 with a `valid_from` PROPERTY
   76 with a `VALID_FROM` EDGE
    0 with both
   17 with neither
(`valid_to`: 6 properties, 2 edges.)

THE SCHEMA DECLARES ONLY THE EDGE. `VALID_FROM` is an edge type, TemporalFact → DesignEpoch (temporal.yaml:103). TemporalFact's declared properties are subject_id, fact_type, statement, value, basis, confidence — there is no `valid_from` among them. `readiness.rs:653` walks the EDGE (`self.outgoing(&fact.node_id, Some(edge::VALID_FROM))`), and grepping the whole workspace for the property name as a string finds NO READER AT ALL. ⇒ The dates on 112 facts — over half the design's time axis — are inert. They render, they export, they look like time bounds, and no computation has ever consulted one.

⭐ THE CAUSE IS A VOCABULARY GAP, NOT CARELESSNESS, and the zero overlap is what proves it. Two populations with two conventions and no node caught between them is not sloppiness — sloppiness would be mixed. `VALID_FROM` demands a DesignEpoch. A writer who has a DATE has nothing to point the edge at, and creating an epoch per date would flood the time axis with points that mark nothing. So they write the date as a property, which the store accepts silently, and get a record that reads correctly to a human and is invisible to every machine. The 76 are facts written by code paths that already had an epoch in hand; the 112 are facts written by hand.

⚠️ THE EXTRACTION HINT DOCUMENTS THE FIELDS THAT DO NOT EXIST. TemporalFact's own hint reads "a requirement creep = a satisfaction fact whose VALID_FROM is a later epoch; a dropped requirement = a fact with VALID_TO set" — phrasing that invites exactly the property form the schema does not declare. The guidance and the schema disagree, and the guidance is what a writer reads.

HOW IT SURFACED: writing `fact:defect-a-property-once-written-cannot-be-removed` returned `"undeclared": ["valid_from"]`. The undeclared-property report (#213) fired on the very node recording an earlier instance of itself, and the second instance was two orders of magnitude larger than the first. See [[fact:defect-a-property-once-written-cannot-be-removed]] — and note that its "NOT ESTABLISHED: whether other node types carry an undeclared property the same way" was answered within one call of being written.

WHAT IS NOT SETTLED, and is the user's to settle: whether the fix is to DECLARE `valid_from`/`valid_to` as date-string properties and teach the readers to prefer the edge and fall back to them; or to keep the edge as the only truth and migrate the 112 (which needs 112 epochs that do not exist); or to let VALID_FROM point at either a DesignEpoch or a date. The first is cheapest and legitimises what people already do; the third makes the edge's `to` polymorphic, which nothing else in the schema is. The 112 are not deletable either way — a property once written cannot be removed.
